searchText: Hello guys, Hope you are all doing well. I have designed a solution that prevents smart contract hacks in a decentralised and reliable manner. I want to ensure that no similar ideas have been proposed in the past and to gauge interest before I write the EIP. to make it short - the solution is a decentralised firewall, part of the execution client, that analyses every transaction for potential hacks. It leverages the EVM to make reverting transactions as transparent and decentralised as possible. I can't think of a way how someone can differentiate between a hack and normal use at code level. 🤔 but interested to know how you approach it.

Hello guys, 

Hope you are all doing well. 

I have designed a solution that prevents smart contract hacks in a decentralised and reliable manner. I want to ensure that no similar ideas have been proposed in the past and to gauge interest before I write the EIP.

to make it short - the solution is a decentralised firewall, part of the execution client, that analyses every transaction for potential hacks. It leverages the EVM to make reverting transactions as transparent and decentralised as possible.
